tasks.short: Review the referral and earlier findings, examine and talk with the patient, decide diagnosis and treatment, and record the diagnosis and plan.

steps.what: Urologist reviews the referral and earlier findings across several screens
Urologist examines and talks with the patient
Urologist diagnoses or treats diseases of genitourinary organs
Urologist records the diagnosis and treatment plan as free text

tasks.design: A visit summary in the record ({OTHER}) shows the referral question, earlier imaging, PSA trend, pathology and treatment together, so the urologist does not open several screens. The urologist writes the diagnosis and plan as today; the code comes from a pick list and a template per common condition gives the standard sections. Examining, diagnosing and treating stay with the urologist; no software proposes diagnoses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings sat in several screens and plans were written as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Records show visit summaries and coded diagnosis lists.
tasks.still_hard: Outside imaging reports arrive as PDFs.
tasks.human_edge: Talking with a man about erectile problems without embarrassment.

evidence.claim: Records can show visit summaries and coded diagnosis pick lists.
Decision software is usually MDR class IIa or higher; here no software proposes diagnoses.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the plan recorded; surgery is outside.
Input contract: earlier findings in the record; fallback is opening each screen.
Examining and diagnosing keep their full time. s1 keeps 60 because the summary gathers what was on several screens; s4 keeps 85 because only finding the code and standard sections go.

incremental.description: Urologist adds a note when no template fits.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new patients with outside findings missing from the summary (s1 keeps 80) and few plans fitting a template (s4 keeps 95) (3.2); high: follow-up patients with long histories in the record (7.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order PSA and other tests, look up earlier PSA values and compute trends, interpret the results, tell the patient, and record the interpretation.

steps.what: Urologist orders diagnostic tests such as PSA: on a form today, from an order set per suspected condition after the change
Urologist checks the final order: patient, tests and clinical question
Urologist signs the checked order, releasing it to the lab
Urologist looks up earlier PSA values and computes PSA trend and density by hand
Urologist interprets the results of diagnostic tests to detect prostate cancer
Urologist tells the patient the results
Urologist records the interpretation as free text

tasks.design: Tests are ordered from order sets per suspected condition in the record ({OTHER}). The record plots all PSA values over time and computes doubling time and PSA density from the prostate volume by fixed formulas, so the urologist does not look up values and calculate by hand. The urologist writes the interpretation as today in a short template. Interpreting results and telling the patient stay with the urologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier PSA values were looked up one by one and trends calculated by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Records plot lab trends and compute fixed formulas.
tasks.still_hard: PSA values from other labs are not in the record.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining an uncertain PSA result to a worried man.
tasks.altitude: The urologist interprets instead of calculating.

reach.learn: Whether trends are clear in letters.

evidence.claim: Records can plot lab trends and compute fixed formulas such as doubling time.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of software in care, including updates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the suspected cancer to the interpretation recorded; biopsy is outside.
Input contract: lab values in the record; fallback is looking up.

Interpreting, telling the patient and checking orders keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 because order sets fill the tests; s2 keeps 20 for reading the plot; s5 keeps 85 because only standard fields go.

incremental.description: Urologist adds outside PSA values to the record.

approvals.approved_version: The test order with patient, tests and clinical question exactly as checked by the urologist in s1c, signed once and released to the lab; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many PSA values come from outside labs and are still looked up (s2 keeps 50), and order sets fit few cases (s1 keeps 80) (11.6); high: surveillance patients with values in the record (21.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review earlier records and letters, take the history, document it, and update the problem and medication lists.

steps.what: Urologist reviews patients' histories in earlier records and letters
Urologist takes the history in conversation
Urologist documents patients' histories

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.check: A validator flags any medication, diagnosis or result not in the record or transcript, and lists every statement that cannot be found in the transcript; the urologist reads the draft against the conversation, resolves each flag and edits the note before saving.
loop.stop: One draft per visit; if the patient declines recording or the draft is rejected, the urologist writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients tell their history in their own words; a form does not capture it.

steps.what: Urologist updates the problem and medication lists by hand

tasks.design: A visit summary in the record ({OTHER}) shows earlier letters, pathology and imaging conclusions together. With consent, a scribe drafts the history note from the consultation; a validator flags medication, diagnoses or results not in the record, and the urologist validates before saving. The medication list is filled from the national medication exchange and confirmed. Taking the history in conversation stays with the urologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier records were read screen by screen and notes typed after visits.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes the clinician validates; records pull medication lists.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add statements the patient did not make.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a patient leaves out about incontinence.
tasks.altitude: The urologist validates drafts instead of typing.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates before the note goes into the record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians reported time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with Tandem notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient visit to lists updated; treatment is outside.
Input contract: patient consent for recording; fallback is typing.

The urologist reads and edits every note. s1 keeps 60 because the summary gathers earlier letters and conclusions; s3 keeps 65 because each draft is read against the conversation and edited; s4 keeps 60 because the medication list fills from the exchange and is confirmed.
research_questions: How long does editing drafted notes take?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients decline recording (s3 keeps 90) and the medication exchange is incomplete (s4 keeps 85) (14.5); high: most visits recorded (25.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose the antibiotic from culture results, look up the guideline and check doses, write the prescription, and administer or apply the treatment.

steps.what: Urologist chooses antibiotics to treat infection based on culture results
Urologist looks up the antibiotic guideline and checks doses and interactions
Urologist writes the antibiotic prescription: line by line today, from the guideline order set after the change
Urologist checks the final prescription: antibiotic, dose, duration and patient against the culture, the guideline and the surveillance alerts
Urologist signs the checked prescription, releasing it to the pharmacy
Urologist administers antiseptics or compresses to treat injury

tasks.design: The hospital's antibiotic guideline is built into order sets per infection type in the prescribing module ({OTHER}), and medication surveillance checks interactions, doses for kidney function and allergies while prescribing, so the urologist does not look them up; the urologist checks the final prescription and signs it once. Choosing the antibiotic and giving treatment stay with the urologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: The guideline and doses were looked up separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Prescribing modules hold guideline order sets and rule-based surveillance.
tasks.still_hard: Resistant infections need a microbiologist's advice.
tasks.human_edge: Judging when a fever means a stone is blocking the kidney.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates; KNMP sets the content.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; software drafts, it does not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: from the infection found to treatment given; microbiology advice is outside.
Input contract: guideline order sets set up; fallback is looking up.

Choosing, checking and signing the prescription stay with the urologist and keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 for reading the guideline advice and alerts; s3 keeps 60 because the order set fills dose and duration.

incremental.description: Urologist reviews alerts that do not apply.

approvals.approved_version: The prescription with antibiotic, dose and duration exactly as checked by the urologist in s3c, signed once for this patient and released to the pharmacy; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex resistant infections fall outside the order sets (s2 keeps 60, s3 keeps 85) (9.4); high: common urinary infections (16.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The urologist keeps examining, diagnosing, interpreting tests and treating; screen searching, hand calculations, typed notes and look-ups shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A urologist with more time for patients.
